name: MMMU
description: MMMU (A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI) is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.

rai:dataCollection: The data for the MMMU dataset was manually collected by a team of over 50 college students from various disciplines, using online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials. The collection process took three stages: (1) selecting 30 subjects from six different disciplines based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in the subjects to provide valuable information; (2) recruiting university students specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary; (3) annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were collected from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data cleaning process involved two steps: (1) lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications; (2) problems were distributed among different co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format; (3) authors categorized the problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, and hard), and approximately 10% of the problems classified as very easy and not aligning with design criteria due to their simplistic nature were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students from various disciplines, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects covered by the benchmark.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to push the boundaries of multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence (AGI). The benchmark aims to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models. The paper discusses the potential for job displacement and economic disruption as AI systems approach Expert AGI, which is defined as reaching at least the 90th percentile of skilled adults in a broad range of tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process, albeit thorough, may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not fully be a sufficient test for Expert AGI.
rai:dataLimitations: Despite its comprehensive nature, MMMU, like any benchmark, is not without limitations. The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not fully be a sufficient test for Expert AGI. However, the authors believe it should be necessary for an Expert AGI to achieve strong performance on MMMU to demonstrate their broad and deep subject knowledge as well as expert-level understanding and reasoning capabilities.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for testing and evaluating multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It is used for benchmarking model performance across various disciplines and assessing capabilities in expert-level perception and reasoning. The dataset includes development, validation, and test splits for few-shot/in-context learning, hyperparameter selection, debugging, and comprehensive evaluation.
